thread.title: All but two Silicon Valley stocks on Bloomberg's tech index are in 'correction' territory

author: Cromwell Schubarth
title: All but two Silicon Valley stocks on Bloomberg's tech index are in 'correction' territory
text: – TechFlash Editor, Silicon Valley   3:03pm PST The Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 index dove into correction territory for the first time in two years on Thursday in a sell-off that swept many Silicon Valley tech stocks along with it. Only two of the 13 tech companies on Bloomberg's Silicon Valley High Technology Index have avoided falling the 10 percent that marks a correction. Three others are in the 20 percent-plus drop territory that marks a bear drop. Here's how how the region's biggest tech stocks, including Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL), Google parent Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG), Facebook (NASDAQ: FB) Intel Corp. (NASDAQ: INTC), Adobe Systems (NASDAQ: ADBE) and Cisco Systems (NASDAQ: CSCO), Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. (NASDAQ: HPE), eBay (NASDAQ: EBAY) and Symantec Corp. (NASDAQ: SYMC) have fared. Some of the Valley's biggest tech companies, including Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD), Applied Materials (NASDAQ: AMAT) and Juniper Networks (NYSE: JNPR), are down double-digit percentages. The sell-off has been prompted by investor anxiety over the prospect of greater inflation, which could lead the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1,032.89 points, or 4.1 percent, to 23860.46 on Thursday. That plunge is the second-steepest point decline on record — topped only by Monday’s 1,175.21-point skid. The S&P 500 decline of 3.8 percent to 2581 on Thursday dropped it more than 10 percent below its record close on Jan. 26. The Nasdaq Composite fell 3.9 percent to 6777 and quite close to correction territory, down 9.7 percent from its high. – TechFlash Editor, Silicon Valley   3:03pm PST Related Content
